response: No, it is not necessary to insert a nasobiliary drainage tube routinely after endoscopic clearance of the common bile duct in patients with choledocholithiasis-induced cholangitis. This procedure is typically reserved for patients with severe or persistent cholangitis, or those who are at high risk of re-obstruction or have significant bile duct damage. Routine use of nasobiliary drainage tubes is not recommended due to the potential risks and discomfort associated with the procedure, as well as the low risk of complications in most patients after successful endoscopic clearance.
